mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative more than 35% of the time despite low FEDFUNDS, or if Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points over three months signals labor market weakness, which may lead to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns in the subsequent 20 days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate increase does not correlate with negative 20-day returns, or if Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in both housing starts (HOUST) and employment (PAYEMS) over three months indicates weakening demand, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as economic growth falters.
failure_condition: If both series decline but 60-day returns are positive more than 65% of the time, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over two months during a late-cycle expansion signals potential supply-side weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decline does not lead to negative returns, or Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the real savings rate (RSAFS) indicates consumers are saving more, leading to reduced consumption and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increase does not correlate with negative 5-day returns, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it may indicate a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS >4.5% does not lead to negative returns, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: If GDP growth (GDPC1) slows to less than 2% annually and unemployment (UNRATE) rises above 5%, it may indicate stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but returns are positive, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in unemployment (UNRATE) during early-cycle expansion may lead to inflationary pressures, prompting tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE drop does not lead to negative returns, or Rank IC < 0.03.
